title: Manage Weaver runs and installation
summary: Inspect, wait for, recover, or cancel a Weaver run; validate generated narrative files; diagnose readiness; or deploy Weaver.
use_when: The sole current Weaver workflow or its exact run ID must be observed, resumed through a new worker process, or cancelled.
Persisted narrative outputs need deterministic validation without a model call.
Weaver private state, Nucleus readiness, installation, or deployment maintenance must be checked or changed.
do_not_use_when: The desired outcome is a new five-stage narrative build; use `weaver.narrative.build`.
The request changes Weaver implementation or contracts rather than operating the installed product.
The request asks for live web interaction, publication, profile editing, or job-application work.
outcome: The selected Weaver run, output tree, readiness condition, or user-owned installation is observed or changed through its supported interface with the exact current record preserved.
effects: `status` and `check` are read-only; `check` invokes no model and does not establish editorial freshness.
`wait` may start a detached replacement worker for a nonterminal run, and `cancel` durably records intent before asking Nucleus to cancel the current stage.
`doctor` may initialize Weaver's private state directory and locks while changing no narrative or current workflow record.
Deployment stages a content-addressed release, coordinates maintenance, changes Weaver's current command and release selectors, and removes only the superseded prototype LaunchAgent when present.
authority: `current.json` is Weaver's sole current operational workflow record; generated files in the narrative repository are the current output authority.
The interactive caller owns the file-access context used by detached Weaver workers, while Nucleus owns the correlated job and authentication state.
Weaver owns its installation and only the installed `providers/weaver` Chancery selector.
success: The selected supported command reports the requested current state and, when an explicit run ID is supplied, does not follow a replacement run.
A recovered worker reuses the exact persisted request and deterministic stage job ID rather than creating another attempt.

A successful deployment validates the installed binary and Nucleus readiness, proves a worker stops under maintenance, removes the exact prototype service when present, publishes Weaver's version-matched Chancery bundle, and ends maintenance.
failure_and_recovery: A Nucleus daemon restart makes an unfinished attempt lost; do not restart Nucleus to recover a Weaver worker.
If deployment fails before commit, the prior Weaver release, command, provider selector, prototype plist, and loaded-service state are restored.
If deployment commits but cannot end maintenance, keep the new release authoritative and end that exact gate through the installed Weaver CLI.
privacy: Weaver private state can contain a complete active stage request and every embedded private input byte; Nucleus retains complete requests and raw protocol output.
Deployment and diagnosis must preserve both state roots and must not expose their contents through Chancery, logs, or public output.
does_not_authorize: Cancelling a run, deploying a release, or removing a prototype service merely because it was inspected.
Deleting `current.json`, generated outputs, Nucleus history, retained release directories, or private logs.
Publication, public-service interaction, or a new terminal-run attempt.

consumers.statement: A current-user operator may inspect, wait for, recover, cancel, or validate a Weaver workflow, diagnose readiness, or explicitly deploy the user-owned installation.
A new narrative build, implementation change, automatic retry, publication workflow, public-service operation, or unscoped process controller is outside this capability.

preconditions.statement: Workflow commands select Weaver private state, the applicable narrative repository, and optionally the exact observed run ID; cancellation and deployment require explicit authority.
Deployment requires a tested absolute Weaver binary, compatible Nucleus readiness, an available maintenance boundary, and ownership of Weaver's existing selectors or their absence.

inputs.statement: Supported inputs are repository and state selectors, an optional exact run ID, a narrative name for check, and an absolute binary plus documented maintenance wait bound for deployment.
Arbitrary process IDs, foreign provider selectors, edited current.json, direct maintenance-file mutation, new model-attempt content, and public-service targets are unsupported inputs.

outputs.statement: Doctor, status, wait, cancel, and check report the exact selected readiness, current-run, terminal, cancellation, or mechanical-validation outcome.

Successful deployment returns a validated content-addressed current release, command and Weaver-owned provider selector, previous selector when applicable, no prototype service, and ended maintenance.

data_semantics.statement: current.json is the sole current workflow record; status is observation, wait is observation plus explicit worker recovery, cancel is durable intent plus one current-stage cancellation request, and check is mechanical validity rather than freshness.
A terminal failed, lost, cancelled, timed-out, malformed, or blocked workflow remains historical current state until an explicit new submission replaces it and is never retried automatically.

identity_and_units.statement: Run ID selects one complete workflow, deterministic stage job ID selects one Nucleus attempt, content hash identifies one installed release, and org.weaver.worker identifies only the removed prototype service.
Nonterminal wait reactivates a worker immediately and every 30 seconds; maintenance begin defaults to a 60-second command bound while deployment supplies its documented update bound.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: An explicit run ID prevents status, wait, or cancel from following a replacement; without it the command selects the sole current record at command time.
Check validates all five persisted outputs and required cross-file invariants; deployment manifests and validates all packaged bytes and installed selectors before commit.
Status is not machine-wide process liveness, check is not repeated editorial review, and deployment does not establish future Nucleus readiness or narrative freshness.

access.statement: Operations run as the current user and access Weaver private state and the selected narrative repository through the interactive process lineage; deployment owns only Weaver installation paths and provider selector.
Weaver does not select unrelated Codex or Nucleus processes, take over foreign selectors, delete retained private state or outputs, or install a resident service.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Status is read-only; wait starts replaceable one-shot workers for the exact durable request; cancel records intent before asking Nucleus and is idempotent for the selected run.

Deployment establishes maintenance, waits for the run lock, stages and validates a release, switches selectors atomically, removes only the exact prototype, and restores all captured pre-commit state on failure.

operational_limits.statement: Weaver supports one current workflow, one run lock, one product installation, no resident daemon or LaunchAgent, and no deletion or automatic terminal-retry interface.
No recovery duration, workflow duration, deployment duration, retained-release count, repository capacity, or service availability objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1 retains exact-run selection, one-attempt recovery, maintenance ordering, content-addressed packaging, and Nucleus invocation protocol 1 compatibility.
A failed pre-commit deployment restores the prior release and selector set; a post-commit failure leaves the new release authoritative and requires maintenance end through that installed CLI.
No perpetual support window for older Weaver releases, private-state formats, macOS behavior, or Nucleus versions is promised.

reliances.statement: Readiness, wait recovery, and cancellation rely on Nucleus for current job and authentication state and exact cancellation behavior.
Mechanical check and workflow recovery rely on the selected narrative repository for the current generated output tree, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes that repository promise.
